entries.canonical_text: I stood motionless. For an hour he sat in bed, listening. At last he groaned softly. Not pain—terror. I knew that sound. I uncovered the lantern. Its narrow beam found the eye. Wide open. A low, quick beating reached me, like a watch wrapped in cotton. His heart! Faster it went, and louder. What if a neighbour heard?

entries.canonical_text: I spoke louder. It grew louder too. I paced and scraped my chair across the boards. Still they chatted. Still they smiled. Louder. Louder! Could you have borne it? They heard! They knew! Their smiles were mocking me. I could bear no more. "I did it!" I screamed. "Tear up the planks! Here! It is the beating of his hideous heart!"
